payload.question:
## Context

tsk-4wf reports fgos approve self-blocking a git merge with local changes would be overwritten by merge: .fgos/events.jsonl (confirmed 4/4 times on 2026-08-21). Research (docs/history/tsk-4wf/RESEARCH.md) found tsk-32v -- a separate item, filed and fixed the SAME night, now status retrospective -- diagnosed the identical symptom via an isolated scratch-repo test and confirmed the real trigger is narrower than tsk-4wf assumed: only a STAGED-but-uncommitted write to that path blocks the merge, not any uncommitted write. The staging came from runOpportunisticMainCheckoutChecks's own git add+git commit step colliding with the callers own lock-holder identity, leaving the file staged when its commit silently failed. tsk-32v shipped the fix directly on main (commit 00aafe0c): the commit now carries the callers lock-holder identity, and any remaining commit failure now runs a git reset to unstage before re-throwing, so the file can no longer be left staged-but-uncommitted by this path. Current source (src/state/events-jsonl-truncation-guard.mjs) confirms both changes are in place today.

## Why this matters

tsk-4wf's own proposed fix (approve self-commits its .fgos/* writes before merging) targets a theory of the bug (any uncommitted write triggers it) that tsk-32v's scratch-repo test disproved -- the actual trigger (a staged-but-uncommitted write) is what tsk-32v's already-shipped fix closes. No incident matching this symptom has landed in this repo's history since commit 00aafe0c. This reads as a duplicate that should close as wontfix/duplicate-of-tsk-32v rather than continue into planning as new work, but closing an item on this evidence is a scope decision for a person, not something discovery decides unilaterally. Please confirm: close tsk-4wf as a duplicate of tsk-32v (already fixed), or is there a live reproduction of this exact error since 2026-08-21 that the research above does not already explain?

payload.answer: Confirmed duplicate of tsk-32v (retrospective, fixed on main commit 00aafe0c, 2026-08-21). Checked the live event log for recurrence since the fix landed: zero recurrences of this exact symptom on .fgos/events.jsonl via approve in 5 days of subsequent activity. (One unrelated recurrence found on 2026-08-24, tsk-3ve/tsk-12o -- different file .fgos/approve-post-success-faults.jsonl, different verb sync-root, different mechanism 'nested-file untracked collision' -- worth its own separate item if not already covered, but out of this item's scope.)
